author: world today news
title: Non-Communicable Diseases and Community Fitness Initiatives in Zimbabwe
text:
• Non-communicable diseases (NCDs) account for about 40% of annual deaths in Zimbabwe.
• NCDs include cardiovascular diseases, diabetes, and certain cancers.
• By 2030, NCDs are projected to surpass communicable diseases as the leading cause of death in sub-Saharan Africa, according to the World Health Organization (WHO).
• Commandos Fitness Club operates in a cemetery in Harare, Zimbabwe, providing a free space for older adults to exercise.
• The club is coached by Joseph Nekati, who started it after his mother suffered a stroke.
• Members, including 64-year-old Susan Gomo, report significant health improvements from regular exercise.
• Gomo has lost weight and improved her mobility while managing high blood pressure and arthritis.
• The Zimbabwean government has introduced a 0.5% tax on certain unhealthy foods in the 2025 national budget to promote healthier dietary choices.
• The tax targets foods like doughnuts, tacos, pizza, hot dogs, shawarma, fries, chicken, and burgers.
• The cemetery has become a safe and serene location for fitness activities, fostering community and health.
• Participants express hopes for proper facilities from the local council to support their fitness initiatives.
